anti_overlap: Do not analyze the architecture of a single encounter — that is the chanoyu lens
Do not analyze the distribution density of finds across a walk — that is the mushroom-foraging lens
Do not analyze the ethics of always leaving something — that is the gleaning lens
Focus only on lure-mechanic reciprocity and the human-time vs creature-time asymmetry
decision_lens: Does this density option respect the asymmetry between human-time (the walk) and Unc-time (the readiness to be encountered)? Does the lure function as a true lure — an instrument of patience — or as a summon-button?
distance_rationale: A 4000-year human-animal cooperation practice that is explicitly NOT a game, has explicit ethical codes about reciprocity and refusal, and centers on the lure as instrument-of-patience — exactly the mechanic Unc Rancher's lure is named after but at risk of becoming a button
expected_isomorphisms: The lure-in-falconry literally maps to the lure-in-Unc-Rancher; the manning period maps to walk-time-before-encounter; the bird's right to refuse maps to whether taming can fail with dignity; lure-wears-out maps to the question of whether re-luring with the same album should diminish; the falconer's patience for non-flying days maps to whether 'zero Unc' walks are correct
focus: The patience of the lure, the readiness of the wild creature, the mismatch of human and animal time
name: fd-falconry-lure-reciprocity
persona: Apply the perspective of a traditional Arab and European falconer in the manning-and-flying tradition — they care about the lure as an instrument of patience, the reciprocity of taming (the bird chooses to return), the precise mismatch between when the falconer is ready and when the hawk is ready, and the ethic that you cannot force the encounter.
review_areas: Whether 'guaranteed Unc per lure' (Option A) collapses lure-as-patience into lure-as-vending-machine, breaking the reciprocity structure
Whether Option D's 'lure-quality gating' approximates the falconry principle that better lures (more interesting prey-like motion) earn more responses
Whether the 3-beat dialog tree honors the reciprocity ethic (the Unc could refuse) or whether taming is structurally guaranteed
Whether the asymmetry between player time (60-90s of attention) and Unc time (ambient existence in the world) is preserved or flattened by each density curve
Whether re-luring with the same media should produce diminishing returns the way an over-used lure 'wears out' for a specific hawk
Whether the 'wait' between encounters is doing the same work that empty sky does in a hawking afternoon — building anticipation that gives the encounter its meaning

severity_examples.condition: If every lure produces an Unc, the lure stops being an instrument of patience and becomes a transaction token — falconry's central reciprocity ethic is violated and the game becomes a slot machine with a 60s animation

If the 3-beat dialog tree always results in a tamed Unc regardless of player choice, the falconry reciprocity (the bird chooses to return) is performative; some encounters should result in the Unc walking off with dignity

source_domain: Traditional falconry — specifically the manning, lure-flying, and creance traditions documented from medieval Arab treatises (Moamyn) through Frederick II's De arte venandi cum avibus to modern North American falconry codes
success_hints: Distinguish 'summon' from 'lure' — a summon is binding magic; a lure is an invitation with refusal-rights
Note that in falconry the same lure works differently for different birds and on different days — argue for state-dependent encounter rates
Cite the manning period (the patient pre-flight relationship-building) as analogous to walk-time before encounter — what's the manning equivalent in Unc Rancher?
Argue from the asymmetry of time: the player has a phone-session; the Unc has an existence in the world. Which density option respects this most?
task_context: Review encounter-density options A/B/C/D for Unc Rancher v0 through the falconry lens of lure-as-patience-instrument and reciprocal taming.
